newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia's Norilsk has no export delay.
newsitem.headline: Russia's Norilsk has no export delay.

text.p: Russia's Norilsk Nickel said on Monday that dockworkers had withdrawn a threat to refuse to load metal for export but warned that tough austerity measures lay ahead.
"I can tell you one hundred percent that dockworkers at Dudinka are loading material as always and that there are no delays," Norilsk spokesman Sergei Vetchinin told Reuters.
He also said RAO Norilsky Nikel management would complete developing a programme by November 1 to raise the company's flagship metals enterprise out of financial crisis.

Norilsk leadership, including chief executive Alexander Khloponin, visited the Arctic town of Norilsk last week to communicate impending austerity measures to workers, but they did not formally meet dockworkers at Dudinka, Norilsk's main export outlet, Vetchinin said.

"But we did meet some members of the workers' collective, explained to them the financial situation, and it was enough for those who were threatening to strike to retract their threat," he said. Khloponin will visit Dudinka in mid-October, he added.

Norilsk is in what Vetchinin said was its second restructuring stage, in which workers not connected to output at the metals combine would be laid off and asked to form private companies to provide Norilsk with services on a competitive basis.
He said 80,000 jobs at the plant, where 40,000 workers are directly involved in metals output, could be at risk, but that only ancillary workers would be laid off.

He also said that the company was focusing on contracts with end-users, including Germany's Krupp Thyssen Nirosta GmbH (KTN), a stainless steel producer grouping Fried Krupp AG Hoesch-Krupp and Thyssen AG.
The Norilsk group's total debts are 13 trillion roubles, including 1.5 trillion roubles in back taxes.
It is owed $200 million from former exporters, Vetchinin said, adding that the enterprise owes its major shareholder, Uneximbank, $210 million.
He said Norilsk plans to issue shares to help pay off debts, but gave no details.

Vetchinin declined to give figures for August and September output and exports, but said production was steady. But Norilsk would tighten up the information it provides on output and exports, he said.
